text:
maria_support: Customer escalated a tool-call failure when using streaming. Model returned a schema validation error: "unexpected end of JSON at position 512". Customer sees the tool args cut off mid-string. Repro attached, severity P2 — asking oncall to triage.

jamie_oncall: can you paste the request_id + the raw streaming chunks? also which model + sdk/version?

maria_support: request_id=rc-89234, model=gpt-stream-4. SDK: redwood-js 0.9.2. Repro curl:
```bash
curl -sS -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses?stream=true \
  -d '{"input":"fetch metadata","tool_call":{"name":"fetch_url","arguments":{ "url":"https://files.example.com/large-manifest.json","opts":{"range":"0-"}}}}'
```
Raw stream fragments they captured (client-side):

chunk1:
data: {"type":"response.delta","delta":{"content":"... calling fetch_url with args:\n{ \"url\": \"https://files.example.com/up\"}"}}

chunk2:
data: {"type":"tool_call","name":"fetch_url","arguments":"{\"url\": \"https://files.example.com/upgrade-manifest/2025-06-0"}

chunk3:
data: {"type":"response.delta","delta":{"content":"...continuing"}}

end:
data: [DONE]

client-side parser fails trying to JSON.parse(arguments) because the string was split and truncated (missing closing braces).

ben_infra: thanks. two quick checks: 1) is there any intermediate proxy (customer side or our gateway) that might be imposing chunk_size limits or dropping mid-body? 2) are we stream-encoding tool_call.arguments as a raw JSON string vs sending structured JSON? If it's serialized into the main event stream as a string, chunk boundaries can break tokens.

lian_eng: looks like the model/service emits the tool_call event and we stream it as plain bytes. If the SDK naively JSON.parse() per-chunk, split tokens will break. We should treat tool_call.arguments as an atomic emission. Options: a) always emit the entire tool_call event in a single server write (atomic). b) augment protocol with an arguments_end sentinel event. c) buffer and reassemble on client side until balanced braces. Short-term patch: buffer chunks for any tool_call event until we see a balanced JSON object before parsing.

jamie_oncall: can we confirm if this is happening inside our edge (nginx) or further upstream? deploy-bot: captured logs for rc-89234: edge-proxy forwarded 200 OK, no 4xx, connection timeouts show none. No obvious truncated body at edge logs.

maria_support: customer confirmed they are hitting directly from browser through our CDN (Fastly) -> edge. They also tested direct curl to api.redwood.ai and saw the same partial split.

ben_infra: if curl sees it too, likely runtime is flushing partial writes. Two hypotheses: runtime writes a long argument string in multiple write() calls and the client assembles them incorrectly; or our streaming layer accidentally trims after a fixed buffer (512 bytes) when serializing tool args. I'll add trace logs around the streaming write path.

lian_eng: I pushed a short experiment branch to buffer tool_call argument bytes until closing brace detection. Also added a regression test that forces chunk boundaries inside strings. If it passes, we'll cut a 0.9.3 hotfix for redwood-js and a server patch to prefer single-write for tool_call events.

maria_support: workarounds for customers?

jamie_oncall: short-term: advise disabling stream=true for requests that rely on tool calls (streaming=false) or base64-encode big string fields so chunk boundaries don't break JSON tokens. Add a KB note: "If using streaming with tool_call, expect args to be buffered until stable — if you see parse errors, set stream=false."

ben_infra: added instrumentation ticket: INF-1728 to log per-write sizes in runtime and to alert if any single logical event is split across >1 kernel write.

lian_eng: plan of record: 1) hotfix client SDK to buffer tool_call args until balanced JSON detected (patch/0.9.3), 2) server-side: attempt single-write for tool_call events and add a unit test to prevent regressions, 3) update docs and support KB, 4) long term: extend streaming protocol to include explicit event delimiters for nested JSON.

maria_support: Thanks — I'll update the customer with the stream=false workaround and ETA for a client hotfix. Marking P2 and linking INF-1728 + repo branch. :thumbsup:
